findings.reason: the build node would pick one of two observables that fail in opposite directions, and only a stated rule (a live observation recorded on the reservation at acquire time, freed when it later disappears) plus a case for the never-observed session makes the constraint implementable and testable.
findings.text: §13's in-harness constraint frees a reservation "when the session its launch was attached to has ended", but nothing on disk records a session's end: the only session-liveness store is the session-host census, whose `live_census` drops a host once its owner process dies and whose per-child entries carry `settled_at` but no end (reckon/crew/session_host.py:272-305, 520-545), while reckon's own reading states that for an in-harness run "liveness belongs to the calling harness, so it is reported as running until a manifest appears" (reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:2157); absence of a record is equally true of a session that never had a host (a `-p` session, or one without the reckon-crew-host plugin), so freed-on-absence would release a live in-harness launch's reservation and reinstate the two-worker race this section exists to close, and freed-only-on-a-positive-stop would leave a killed in-harness launch in such a session stranded — the defect the arm was added to repair; the case list exercises only the ended direction, so the gate cannot tell which observable the node implemented

findings.reason: without that control the terminal-phase arm of the freeing rule is unmeasured, so a gate could pass while the arm that keeps a finished in-harness run launchable does not fire.
findings.text: the case "a finished in-harness launch of an existing run id leaves the run launchable" is reddened by no listed negative control: the control that used to cover it (freeing an in-harness reservation by the dispatching process's liveness) was replaced by the ended-session control, and a mutation that frees an in-harness reservation on session end only — never on a terminal phase — passes every named control while reddening this case

response_events.note: §13 no longer reserves for in-harness launches: no store records a session's end, and reckon reads an in-harness run's liveness as the calling harness's, so an in-harness relaunch takes no reservation and is refused while a CLI launch holds one.
